question: How do I turn on Android's predictive back animation for my app?
reference_answer: In android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml, add android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback="true" to the <application> tag (requires Android 13 or later).

question: Is there a command to hide the red DEBUG ribbon while I'm debugging in VS Code?
reference_answer: Use the 'Toggle Debug Mode Banner' debug command (Command Palette or Flutter inspector); it hides the debug banner even when running a debug build.

question: My app loses its state whenever the OS restarts it. Where do I learn how to restore it?
reference_answer: See the 'Restore state on Android' and 'Restore state on iOS' pages, which explain how to restore app state after a restart.

question: What are the pillars of Flutter's security strategy?
reference_answer: Five pillars: Identify, Detect, Protect, Respond and Recover.

question: Can Dart code keep running when my app isn't in the foreground, and how is that set up?
reference_answer: Yes. Set up an isolate for background execution using callbacks and a callback dispatcher; the WorkManager plugin adds persistent background tasks that survive app restarts and reboots.

question: In the SQLite to-do example, how does each new item get its id?
reference_answer: The id column is declared as INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, so the database assigns a new id on every insert and the insert method returns a Todo with that generated id.

question: How do I run staging and production variants of my app on Windows desktop?
reference_answer: Pass the flavor flag: flutter run -d windows --flavor staging (or production). It works on Windows without any CMake configuration.

question: What's the right way to remove the Flutter SDK from my machine?
reference_answer: Delete the flutter directory you installed Flutter into (for example rm -rf on macOS/Linux or Remove-Item on Windows).

question: How can I get crash reports from my users' devices into a monitoring dashboard?
reference_answer: Create a report containing the error and its stack trace and send it to an error-tracking service such as Sentry, Crashlytics, Bugsnag, Datadog or Rollbar. The recipe uses Sentry: get a DSN, import the package, initialize the SDK and capture errors programmatically.

question: What's the best way to put together a minimal reproduction when filing a Flutter bug?
reference_answer: Create a minimal Flutter app that shows the problem (run flutter create bug and edit main.dart, or use DartPad) and paste it into the GitHub issue; for larger repros upload a separate repository and link it.

question: Is there a tool that automatically updates code that uses deprecated Flutter APIs?
reference_answer: Yes, the flutter fix tool that ships with Flutter suggests and applies changes for deprecated APIs. It is available from the command line and integrated into Android Studio/IntelliJ (quick-fixes) and VS Code (code actions).

question: How do I set up ChromeDriver to run Flutter integration tests in a browser?
reference_answer: Install it with npx @puppeteer/browsers install chromedriver@stable, add its directory to your PATH, then verify with chromedriver --version.

question: What does json_serializable generate for me so I don't write serialization code by hand?
reference_answer: A source code generator creates a file such as user.g.dart that contains all the necessary serialization logic, so you can forget manual JSON serialization in the class; the calling API (jsonDecode/jsonEncode) stays the same.

question: What are the steps for generating type-safe platform bindings with Pigeon?
reference_answer: Create the Pigeon definition file in Dart (with @HostApi/@FlutterApi annotations), run the generator, implement the generated native interface on each platform, then call the API from Flutter.

question: Which command produces an App Store-ready bundle for my iOS app, and where does the output go?
reference_answer: Run flutter build ipa; it creates an .xcarchive in build/ios/archive/ and an App Store .ipa bundle in build/ios/ipa.

question: Which system packages do I need on Ubuntu before installing Flutter?
reference_answer: curl, git, unzip, xz-utils, zip and libglu1-mesa, installed with apt-get install.

question: What do I need to host so Android opens my app instead of the browser for a web link?
reference_answer: An assetlinks.json file hosted on a domain you own, containing your app's package name and the sha256 fingerprint of the signing key used to build the APK.

question: How can I restrict a text field to 5 characters?
reference_answer: Set the TextField's maxLength property (the tutorial sets it to 5 because the game only allows 5-letter guesses).

question: When adding Flutter to an existing Android app, should I use FlutterFragment or FlutterActivity?
reference_answer: Use a FlutterFragment when you want Flutter inside a modular piece of UI (drawer, tabs, a ViewPager page); if an Activity fits your needs, a FlutterActivity is quicker and easier to use.

question: Where should I start if I want a cloud database for my Flutter app?
reference_answer: Start with the Firebase resources: add Firebase to your Flutter app and get started with Cloud Firestore (or Firebase SQL Connect).

question: How does a user type a line break in the AI chat prompt box on a phone versus a desktop?
reference_answer: On mobile, tap the Return key on the virtual keyboard; on web and desktop, press Shift+Enter.

question: How do I keep my Play Store service account credentials safe when building on a CI server?
reference_answer: Don't leave credentials on the ephemeral server; store them in the CI system's encrypted environment variables and pass them to the build with --dart-define, taking care not to echo them to the console.

question: My animations look janky. What should I check first when profiling?
reference_answer: Make sure you profile an app built in profile mode, because the default debug mode isn't indicative of release performance. Then look for UI rebuilt far more than expected and large lists built directly instead of with ListView.

question: How do I feed audio data into a stream while using flutter_soloud?
reference_answer: Create a buffer stream with SoLoud.instance.setBufferStream, play it, call SoLoud.instance.addAudioDataStream(stream, audioChunk) as data arrives, and mark the end with setDataIsEnded.

question: What do the colored bars in DevTools' Flutter frames chart show?
reference_answer: Each bar set is one Flutter frame, color-coded to show the work done on the UI thread and on the raster thread.

question: Which accessibility standards and regulations might apply to my Flutter app?
reference_answer: WCAG 2 (the W3C web content accessibility standard), EN 301 549 (the European ICT accessibility standard), and the VPAT template for documenting conformance.

question: How do I find AI skills that a package I just added ships with?
reference_answer: Run the skills CLI with dart run skills@ get; library authors can bundle official skills directly inside their packages.

question: In my iOS App Clip target, what do I add to Build Phases so the Dart code gets compiled?
reference_answer: Add a new Run Script Phase below Dependencies containing /bin/sh "$FLUTTER_ROOT/packages/flutter_tools/bin/xcode_backend.sh" build, and uncheck 'Based on dependency analysis'.

question: How do I use a custom font throughout my app?
reference_answer: Add the font files as assets, declare them under flutter: fonts: in pubspec.yaml with a family name, then set fontFamily in a TextStyle (or the app theme).

question: How do I read the text a user has typed into a text field?
reference_answer: Create a TextEditingController, attach it to the TextField through its controller property, and read controller.text; dispose of the controller when done.

question: How do I let users swipe a list item away to delete it?
reference_answer: Wrap each list item in a Dismissible widget with a unique key and an onDismissed callback that removes the item from the data source.

question: How do I show a brief message at the bottom of the screen after an action?
reference_answer: Use ScaffoldMessenger.of(context).showSnackBar with a SnackBar widget.

question: What's the efficient way to display a list with thousands of items?
reference_answer: Use ListView.builder, which builds items lazily as they scroll into view instead of creating all children up front.

question: How do I make a list scroll sideways instead of vertically?
reference_answer: Set scrollDirection: Axis.horizontal on the ListView.

question: How do I add a slide-out side navigation menu to a screen?
reference_answer: Add a Drawer widget to the Scaffold's drawer property, filled with a ListView of items (DrawerHeader and ListTiles); close it with Navigator.pop.

question: How can I save a small value like a counter so it survives app restarts?
reference_answer: Use the shared_preferences package to store key-value data on disk (for example setInt and getInt).

question: How do I connect my app to a WebSocket server and listen to messages?
reference_answer: Add the web_socket_channel package, connect with WebSocketChannel.connect, listen to channel.stream (for example with a StreamBuilder), send with channel.sink.add, and close the sink when done.

question: How do I fade a widget in and out?
reference_answer: Use AnimatedOpacity: wrap the widget and change its opacity value with setState, with a duration for the animation.

question: How do I define app-wide colors and text styles that widgets can reuse?
reference_answer: Set a ThemeData on MaterialApp's theme (colors and text styles) and read it in widgets with Theme.of(context).

question: How do I update my Flutter SDK to the newest version?
reference_answer: Run flutter upgrade, which updates the SDK on the current channel.

question: How do I fetch a list of items from a REST API and show it in a scrollable list?
reference_answer: Add the http package, fetch the JSON and convert the response into Dart objects (fetch data recipe), then display the items lazily with ListView.builder (long lists recipe).

question: How do I open a new screen with some data and get a value back when it closes?
reference_answer: Pass the data to the new screen (through its constructor or route arguments) when calling Navigator.push, and return a result by passing it to Navigator.pop; await the push future to receive it.

question: What are my options for storing data on the device, and how do I save a simple setting?
reference_answer: The choose-a-database page compares storage options such as SQLite and cloud databases; for a simple setting use the shared_preferences package to store a key-value pair on disk.

question: How do I test a widget that depends on a network call without hitting the real server?
reference_answer: Use Mockito to create a mock of the HTTP client or service and stub its responses, then pump the widget inside testWidgets and verify the result with finders.

question: How do I set up separate dev and production builds for both Android and iOS?
reference_answer: On Android define productFlavors in the Gradle configuration; on iOS create schemes and build configurations in Xcode; then run or build with --flavor <name>.

question: How do I add a custom typeface and make it the default text style for the whole app?
reference_answer: Declare the font in pubspec.yaml (fonts recipe), then set fontFamily in the app's ThemeData text theme so all text uses it (themes recipe).

question: How do I find out what is making my release build large?
reference_answer: Build with the --analyze-size option to produce a size breakdown (measuring app size page) and explore it visually with the DevTools app size tool.

question: My app stutters while scrolling. How do I profile it and what general practices help?
reference_answer: Profile in profile mode (not debug) with the DevTools Performance view to see UI and raster thread work per frame, and follow the performance best practices such as avoiding unnecessarily large rebuilds.

question: How do I add a Flutter module to an existing iOS app and debug it?
reference_answer: Integrate the Flutter module into the iOS project (CocoaPods or the documented project setup), then debug by launching the host app and running flutter attach.

question: How do I make a web link open a specific screen in my Android app?
reference_answer: Handle deep links in the app's routing (deep linking page) and set up Android App Links by hosting an assetlinks.json file for your domain (app links recipe).

question: How do I organize my app into layers and share state between screens with ChangeNotifier?
reference_answer: Follow the architecture guide's layered (MVVM-style) structure, and share state by exposing a ChangeNotifier that screens listen to, as in the simple app state management page.

question: How do I publish to Google Play and automate the release process?
reference_answer: Build and sign an Android app bundle and upload it to the Play Store (Android deployment page); automate it with continuous delivery tooling such as fastlane (CD page).

question: How do I validate a form and also read what the user entered?
reference_answer: Wrap fields in a Form with a GlobalKey and give each TextFormField a validator (validation recipe); read the entered text with a TextEditingController (retrieve input recipe).

question: How do I keep heavy JSON parsing from freezing the UI?
reference_answer: Move the parsing to a separate isolate (compute or Isolate.run) so it doesn't block the UI thread; the background parsing recipe shows it and the isolates page explains why.

question: How do I support screen reader users and verify that my app works with them?
reference_answer: Make sure the UI exposes semantics so screen readers can describe it (assistive technologies page), and test it with tools such as Accessibility Scanner on Android and Accessibility Inspector on iOS (accessibility testing page).
